title: White Blast Tops South Korea's Box Office, Ending Chiikawa's Five-Week Reign
excerpt:
South Korean mystery thriller White Blast led the weekend with $2.3 million.
Chiikawa dropped to second after five weeks at the top.
body_md:
South Korea's box office changed leaders over the November 20–22, 2026 weekend as Showbox's snowbound mystery thriller White Blast debuted at No. 1. Its arrival ended a five-week stretch at the top for the Japanese animated hit Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island. The result highlighted the ability of a locally produced suspense film to compete with an unusually durable imported animation success.

According to KOBIS, the tracking service run by the Korean Film Council, White Blast earned approximately $2.3 million from 310,890 admissions on 1,244 screens over the weekend. That represented 39.6 percent of the weekend market. Since opening midweek on November 18, the film has accumulated $3.1 million from 423,196 admissions. These figures describe the South Korean theatrical market rather than a worldwide total.

The film is co-directed by Hong Eui-jeong, whose previous work includes Voice of Silence, and Park Sun-woo, and is adapted from a stage play. Kim Yoon-seok plays a station master preparing to retire from an isolated rural railway station, while Koo Kyo-hwan portrays his newly arrived replacement. A severe snowstorm cuts the station off just as reports emerge that a prison bus has overturned. When the men find a body inside a railway tunnel, their growing suspicion of each other turns the remote setting into the center of a tense mystery.

Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island took second place in its eighth weekend, earning $695,853 from 91,328 admissions on 746 screens. Directed by Kei Oikawa and based on Nagano's manga, the fantasy adventure has now passed three million admissions in South Korea. Since its September 30 release, it has grossed $23.8 million from 3,069,422 viewers. Moving down a place therefore does little to diminish the scale of its established theatrical run.

Lionsgate's The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened in third with $471,769 from 59,014 admissions. The survival thriller sequel Fall 2: Deadpoint ranked fourth with $405,611. A concert film celebrating singer Lim Young-woong's tenth anniversary took fifth by admissions, attracting 31,535 viewers across just 154 screens, but its $676,840 revenue was the second-highest dollar total of the weekend. The distinction matters because the admissions ranking and the revenue ranking were not identical.

The theatrical rerelease of Damien Chazelle's La La Land placed sixth, collecting $182,612 in its second weekend back in cinemas. Other titles in the top ten included Final Interview, Maca and Roni The Movie, Detective Conan: The Counterfeit Case of Ultra 30, and The Cat in the Hat. Taken together, the South Korean box office generated approximately $6 million over the weekend, up from $4.8 million in the preceding frame.

White Blast has made a strong opening statement, but its first weekend alone cannot establish how long it will remain on top. The next several frames will show whether its claustrophobic premise and local appeal can sustain audience interest against returning animated favorites and newly released international franchises.
seo_title: White Blast Leads Korea Box Office as Chiikawa Slips
seo_description: White Blast opens at No. 1 in South Korea with $2.3 million, ending Chiikawa's five-week run at the top of the weekend chart.
